semantic_correction.stem: A client receiving chronic dialysis says, 'My laboratory results look acceptable, but dialysis has disrupted my work, relationships, sleep, and mood.' Which nursing response best reflects comprehensive dialysis care?

options.A: Assess the physical, emotional, social, and role effects of dialysis, then share the findings with the interdisciplinary team to individualize the client's plan of care.
options.B: Concentrate the plan on dialysis adequacy and laboratory goals, and address work, relationships, sleep, or mood if those concerns later interfere with treatment.
options.C: Use the facility's standard psychosocial plan for dialysis clients, because consistent care is preferable to changing the plan for individual role or emotional concerns.
options.D: Postpone psychosocial assessment until physical dialysis goals are unmet, then consider social-work input if problems with daily functioning continue.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services guidance for ESRD facilities requires an individualized comprehensive assessment and an individualized comprehensive plan of care developed by the interdisciplinary team. The assessment includes psychosocial needs, the client's abilities, interests, preferences, goals, support systems, physical activity, and other factors affecting care. The plan of care must address psychosocial status through appropriate monitoring and social-work interventions, including counseling or referrals when indicated, and CMS requires use of a standardized mental and physical assessment tool selected by the social worker at regular intervals or more often when needed. CMS also states that rehabilitation planning should support the level of productive activity desired by the patient and includes quality-of-life education within the plan. National Kidney Foundation guidance independently recognizes that dialysis can affect physical health, mood, relationships, independence, daily functioning, treatment adherence, and overall quality of life. Therefore acceptable laboratory values do not eliminate the need to assess and incorporate physical, emotional, social, role, and treatment-burden effects into an individualized interdisciplinary plan. B is incorrect because psychosocial concerns are part of comprehensive dialysis care and do not need to wait until they disrupt treatment. C is incorrect because CMS requires individualized care planning rather than a fixed psychosocial response. D is incorrect because psychosocial assessment and social-work involvement are routine components of dialysis care and are not contingent on failure to meet physical treatment goals.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Include physical, emotional, social, role-function, and treatment-burden effects in ongoing dialysis assessment and communicate these findings to the interdisciplinary team for an individualized plan of care.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the absolute-word and answer-length cues, rebuilt all four responses to comparable length and specificity, freshly verified current CMS ESRD assessment/plan-of-care requirements with NKF corroboration, and made individualized interdisciplinary psychosocial care the single best response despite acceptable laboratory results.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests comprehensive individualized dialysis care beyond laboratory targets with one clearly best response, balanced alternatives, current federal requirements, and no absolute-word or answer-length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reflects CMS-required individualized interdisciplinary assessment and care planning that incorporates psychosocial, role, and quality-of-life effects of dialysis.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Psychosocial concerns are part of comprehensive ESRD care and should not be deferred until they begin interfering with treatment or laboratory goals.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CMS requires an individualized comprehensive plan of care based on the client's assessment, preferences, goals, support systems, and changing condition.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Psychosocial assessment and social-work interventions are routine components of dialysis care and do not depend on physical treatment goals first becoming unmet.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely integrates multidimensional assessment with individualized interdisciplinary planning; B delays psychosocial care, C substitutes a standardized plan for individualized assessment, and D incorrectly makes psychosocial assessment contingent on physical-treatment failure.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel dialysis care-planning responses of comparable length and specificity; the prior 'only' distractors and uniquely-long correct response were removed.
